title: Quick, easy, blendable & at drugstore prices....gotta love it!!
text: I think we all have days where we're looking for something quick and easy when it comes to makeup.  Anything to get us out the door looking somewhat put together with the least amount of time involved is the goal.  If you're looking for a quick eyeshadow look that takes next to no time these are one answer.  Cream eyeshadow on one end and a brush on the other.  The brush is surprisingly usable, but since I've got older eyes (which means older skin that needs to be babied) I just use one of mine.  They go on pretty smooth and creamy.  Not a ton of pigment on the first pass, but it's very buildable.  The swatches on my arm are 2 passes of each color.  They also blend out really well.  I put a couple passes on my lower lid and blend it up into my crease and I'm good to go.  There is a bit of shimmer in this one, but it's not overwhelming.  Just a bit of sparkle that looks good even on aging eyes.  They make it through the whole day, but I did notice some creasing and breakdown after about 6-8 hours.  Not a lot, just enough to be noticeable.  Overall these were pretty impressive and I think they'd also be great for someone who was just getting into makeup too.

title: This was kind of a "gimmicky" fail for me.
text: Generally, I love EasyDew products and they always seem to deliver what they promise.  That said, this product was a serious letdown and a bit gimmicky, in my opinion.  The delivery system of the product was completely unnecessary and did absolutely nothing to help with product placement.  The use of growth factor along with the claims to provide filling of lines and wrinkles instantly was where my disappointment came in.  Mostly because it did NOT do what it claimed.  The product is a clear gel that absorbs into the skin and does provide some hydration.  However, I think that's mostly down to the use of the hyaluronic acid it contains, which becomes a problem for me to use in my daytime skincare because I live in an absurdly DRY climate in the winter months and hyaluronic acid without access to moisture in the air or in the form of other products means it's going to suck the moisture from the surrounding tissues.....which means you end up with a VERY dry, wrinkly looking area anywhere you put this.  As for the EGF it contains, there are some studies that show it does help with repeated use OVER TIME, but it does not magically erase lines and wrinkles, and certainly not in the formulation offered here.  I feel like it's a case of a very good company, with very good skincare products that sadly made a mistake in caving into the "quick fix" trend so many other companies have.  This was a definite miss for me.

title: Loaded with hydration & plant extracts that my skin NEEDS during the winter months!!
text: These masks have become a favorite this fall and winter when my skin needs an extra dose of hydration.  I've just turned 50 and it's a constant battle to keep my skin hydrated just due to the aging process.  When you add in cold, dry air outside and hot, dry air inside it just makes it so much more difficult.  I've been adding masks to my skincare routine this winter and they've made a huge difference.  I try to do at LEAST one a week, but as it gets colder I've been using them every few days.  I'll use them at night after I've cleansed and used my prescription skincare and then I'll follow up with my nightly routine.  I love all of the plant extracts loaded into this one along with the niacinamide and hyaluronic acid.  One thing to keep in mind though is that if you're using this (or anything with hyaluronic acid, really) and you're in a dry climate you need to make sure you provide additional moisture for the HA to bind to.  It's why I use this one at night since I keep a humidifier running on my bedside table that pumps that moisture into the air.  In addition to the hydration it also does a great job of noticeably minimizing the appearance of some of larger pores on my face which of course makes my skin look firmer and smoother.

title: I've found the BEST BB CREAMS from Korean beauty brands & this is no exception!!
text:
So, I'm recently 50 (I'm wondering how long I'll keep adding recently to my age??) and during 2020 I fell in love with Korean skin care and Korean BB Creams. This one gets high marks, and it's a bit different than the others I've tried.

I ordered the lightest shade since I'm VERY fair and it worked perfectly. That's one of the things I love about BB Creams in general, they provide coverage but they also seem to work with your skin tone rather than masking it. This applied beautifully with a brush and my fingers (my preferred method). I'm assuming it would work with a damp sponge, as well. On me that tends to look cakey for some reason, so I don't generally go that route. It worked well over multiple moisturizers and both of my favorite sunscreens. I use a primer occasionally and had no problems with application when I did. It goes on smoothly and blends out easily. It's a very light formula and feels like I'm not even wearing makeup. It doesn't have a high amount of coverage. I would call it a buildable medium, as far as that goes. Now, here's where it differs from the other Korean BB Creams I've tried.....it dries down to a very satin, skin like finish. Most others end up with either a dewy or slightly luminous finish, which is fine. This is the first one I've found that doesn't. It's definitely not a matte finish, though.

It wears really well. I can get a full 10 hours of wear out of it, whether I set it or not. That's another thing about the way this drys down, if you tend toward dry skin (I do) then you can get away with not powdering this one if that's your preference. When I do use powder I go in pretty lightly, and usually just in the areas where my pores might be having a particularly "showy" day with a blurring powder. The bonus that seems to come with most Korean beauty facial products is the SPF. This is a PA+++/SPF 50+. Now that doesn't mean I skip my normal sunscreen, cause you're never gonna convince me that what you get in foundation or BB Cream is adequate protection.....but I will never say no to MORE protection. EVER.

This is a beautiful BB Cream that works really well on aging skin, so I imagine it would be a dream on younger skin, perfect or textured alike. One other thing I noticed is that at the end of the day I still hardly noticed I was wearing makeup. And when I washed it off my skin felt and looked pretty good. It wasn't dried out and didn't have that worn out look that I've gotten used to seeing after a full day in makeup. Definitely a keeper!!

title: It definitely helps correct skin tone differences & does smooth pores in SOME areas.
text:
I got this in Nude. I have some areas in my face that have some sun damage, some broken capillaries, and some enlarged pores. The only thing that I've found that covers these completely is concealer for the first two, only two primers do the job on the pores that I've found. I figured this might give me some additional coverage due to the nude tint so maybe I could skip the concealer and just go with foundation for coverage. I was also hoping it would be another primer that would blur/fill the pores and not just "disappear" after foundation gets applied.

I was actually impressed by the tone correction I got from this. It's not a concealer (obviously), so I wasn't expecting full coverage. I was just looking for a muting of the redness & the sun spots so I could maybe skip the concealer. It did exactly that. It provided a veil of nude tint that made my areas of sun damage and sun spots (yeah, they're freckles) almost disappear. The redness was muted somewhat. Enough that I when I skipped the concealer I was pretty happy with the result I got from just this product under my foundation. That being said, it doesn't play well with every foundation. I noticed that it doesn't seem to work as well with my dewy/hydrating foundations. That may just be a "me thing", but I thought I'd throw it out there for consideration.

So, this leads to the pore filling/smoothing. It does smooth out some areas with pores and it does continue to do that after the foundations is applied.....in some areas. Which seem to be in the areas that don't move a lot. So on my face, I have enlarged pores on the side of my nose in the nostril area and down toward my mouth, on my chin, and on my forehead in the center. Now, everyone's face moves but we don't all emote with our faces in the same areas. I tend to have a very expressive mouth and I arch one eyebrow a lot. I don't furrow or wrinkle my forehead much. The primer didn't hold up on my chin or around the nostrils and down toward my mouth. The center of the forehead held up perfectly.
So, while I like this primer for the tone correction, I need something that smooths my pores in all areas of my face. If you're just looking for a good primer to even out your skin tone or provide some base color correction I would absolutely recommend this one. The pore thing....I think that's going to be something that depends on the person. This definitely has a place in my makeup routine. I can use it in the areas where I need the tone correction and use something else for my problem pore areas. It's perfect for my light makeup days and I'm going to try it with just some light powder on my next "no makeup" makeup day.

title: It works really well, just not for what I had bought it for….
text:
This thing is REALLY long. One side is rounded dimples, the other side is raised brush-type projections. Bought it for my husband’s shower because it looked fairly indestructible and he seems to be able to destroy pretty much any type of back scrubber. This thing is thick, has some heft to it, and has sturdy grips at either end. My husband was definitely more impressed with this one than some of the others I’ve handed to him for use in the shower.

So, after his first shower with it I asked him how it went. He looks at me and says “I’m not sure I’m using it the right way, but it works pretty good.” And that was his idea of providing feedback on how it worked. Of course, that’s not enough….especially when it starts with I’m not sure if I’m using it right. Turns out (after tons of questioning, Good Lord it’s like bath scrubbers had suddenly become highly confidential state secrets) that it didn’t work all that well as a back scrubber for him. He didn’t like that you have to lather up your back with a loofah or washcloth first and then use the back scrubber. He tried to put soap on the scrubber and use it to wash his back but the soap just ran down between the scrubbers and he couldn’t build a lather up. So he tossed it on the shower floor and was going to tell me that it didn’t work. But then he decided to see if it would work to remove the callused skin on his feet. Apparently it did. He started by just leaving it on the floor of the shower and rubbing his feet back and forth on it, and that worked well. But then he grabbed the handles and put some tension on it with his foot and moved it by using the handles. Apparently this worked VERY well. So well that he had brought up the brush he usually uses in the shower for his feet and threw it in the garbage. (He said it needed replacing anyway.) He wants to keep this one in the shower to keep using it on his feet & is completely excited that he doesn’t have to bend over and contort himself while scrubbing his feet anymore. He still needs me to find a back scrubber though…….

title: This is LITERALLY a sun-kissed look in a bronzer.  So freakin' pretty on the skin....
text:
Ya know how product descriptions are usually a bunch of marketing hype that you just kind of blow by....like blah, blah, blah natural, blah blah blah 10 years younger. Or whatever. So the point is that I was writing this review and I had used the words "sun-kissed" twice (I took one out). Then I looked at the product description and I was like....well, crap. That's what they literally said it would look like. So here's the details:

It is a highly pigmented powder that blends out beautifully and is easily buildable. Not an in-your-face blinding shimmer, more of a sun-kissed shimmer that looks natural on the skin. The color 02 bronzed euphoria looks like you’ve gotten a light tan with a little bit of pink undertone. (I’m fair skin, strawberry blonde, blue eyes for reference.) Kind of like what would happen if you actually WENT into the sun. Without SPF. Which, of course, you shouldn’t do. Like, ever. I also handed it off to my 18 year old daughter and her opinion was the same as mine.....right down to the slightly pinkish undertone. We would both put this on "summer makeup must-have" list.

title: WORTH THEY BUY!
text:
First off and to the bottom line, for quality and price point totally WORTH THE BUY!!

For reference, I ordered the 22 inch Color #2 Darkest Brown. I am 5'11" and ordered a length similar to my own hair.

Now for the background: I am mid 40s and I have always had SUPER thick, curly hair until an autoimmune thing kicked in at which point I lost 3/4s of that volume over a year. So I've been playing around with hair extensions. If we can dye out grays, do our nails, etc. to feel better about ourselves, why not hair extensions?? This particular piece is AMAZING! Honestly, it could be thicker, but then I feel it would be too heavy. It's perfect for me.

The color matches perfectly. The length is accurate. The sheen is beautiful. Some other reviewers complained about it tangling, and although it does, it doesn't tangle more than my own hair and brushes out back to original form with ease. ...Some other reviewers said it doesn't stay in place and I personally disagree. I straighten my hair, put it up in a ponytail at the height I want, clip in the extension, wrap the extra piece and secure with 3-4 bobby pins around the base. That may sound like a lot of work, but really it isn't (especially since I only wash my hair every third day or so, and in between days, I just shower without wetting my hair). It took me a couple tries to perfect it, but since, I have it down and wear it for 12-14 hours continuously without an issue. No headache, no slipping. My hair blends with the extension and you can't tell which strands are "real". ...Admittedly, I haven't played around with curling it or anything so I can't commit or advise on that.

All in all, I feel this is a cheap, quick and easy way to feel beautiful. And everyone deserves to feel beautiful! Hope this review helped :)

title: A product designed the way it should be!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
text:
Over the past few years many razor mfg's have moved their mfg to china.... I'm not saying this is bad or good, but china mfg typically has a 15% defect (their QA) at the consumer level.... and if you look at the majority of razor reviews, they fall right into that category. Although the product design may be the same, production related QA is far from good....and I have had my share of this type of crap from a variety of name brand mfg's.
This razor is designed and built the way they use to be..... To start with, the design holds and positions the blades to ensure it is always set at the nest angle for shaving the closest. 2ndly, the weight of the razor is well balanced and the handle design places your thumb/finger at the perfect pivot/handling point consistently and precludes slipping or re-adjusting you hand. Other companies attempt to use surface-design/pattern to hold your contact point in place, but in doing so this also slows/restricts the pivoting/movement of the head which induces razor burn/nicks/cuts! The other item that is definitely mentionable is the ability to clean the razor...it's great!!!! It is the 1st razor I have ever owned that you can effectively rinse all of the shaving particulates out of without disassembly!!!! The design is so good, that my 1st test was to do a dry shave with no water, etc. It performed excellent (and I have a tough beard)… I have now shaved with hot water, etc. twice like you are suppose to and the shave is as close as one can get to a straight-edge.... excellent product!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

title: It’s got a thick gooey consistency and spreads pretty easily. Bare in mind that the thinner you ...
text:
This product gets a lot of mixed reviews and that’s probably because people have the wrong idea as to what this mask actually does. At first my expectations were completely off too. It’s a peel off mask so I’m expecting to pull something out expect “What? It didn’t pull anything out at all!” However, the one thing that made me rethink this mask was that even though it didn’t pull anything physical out of my face I did notice these tiny little white spots on the peeled mask and at first I thought they were air bubbles. The next time I used it, I made sure I didn’t have any air bubbles, one slick, black, mask. When I peeled it off again, there they were! Little white spots that are slightly translucent, then it finally clicked. This mask is called Sebum Out! It says nothing about blackheads or whiteheads removal, its meant to tackle sebum (precursor to black/white heads) which is oily/waxy so if the mask is to pull anything out… it’s not going to be anything with a physical shape hence those translucent little spots!

Now with that cleared up, it’s a totally different kind of review! It is very soothing. It’s got a thick gooey consistency and spreads pretty easily. Bare in mind that the thinner you apply this on your face the harder it is to take off. My rule is to apply enough that I no longer see my skin tone coming from underneath the mask. It’s shiny black and smells somewhat minty but very light and the rest of the scent borders medicinal/earthy which isn’t bad or anything. After you apply it, its very cooling and minty. It takes a bit of time to dry completely especially if some areas have a thicker application. The peeling process is pretty painless and easy, slow and steady though. Overall it’s a pleasant experience. I use this mainly for my troubled areas (nose, chin, and T-zone)

title: Polished every day!
text:
My family has several different Oral B electric toothbrush models. All give us that just polished feeling that one gets at the dentist! I prefer the models that have the 2 min auto timer, as it encourages spending that extra time to get all surfaces clean. The electric unit and timer are particularly useful for young children and older folks who may be suffering with limited hand dexterity due to arthritis and sore joints. I have given up manual toothbrushes forever and even take the Oral B when I travel. A full charge will easily last a week.

I have noticed the children have fewer new cavities when they use their electric Oral B. It also promotes healthy gums. Although we were able to share one base unit with our own individual brush heads at home, each child was sent away to college with a new electric Oral B to maintain that dentist visit polish every day! My daughter prefers this model with the dual brush heads. She feels it cleans more efficiently than the single head.

Of course the unit and brush heads cost more than a manual brush, but for sparkling teeth, fewer cavities, healthy gums, fresher breath--a real bargain!

Tips for using - I found you're better off with dry hair. When the hair's wet, it's harder for the vacuum to pull it in. I also found that the vacuum works much better on longer hair then on shorter hair. Maybe the shorter hairs are too light and get blown around? Last but not least, watch out for the settings. The dial goes 1-9 so I started with 4, which was way too short. I could have grown that beard from scratch in a couple of weeks. 5 also proved a little short for me. Be sure to start a lot higher than you think you need, and work your way down if needed.

title: Superb product
text:
I've been using brand X for years, and liked it, but like everyone else resented that the battery determined its useful life. I decided to try a battery operated unit with which I could use rechargeable NiMH batteries. I got my hands on both brands and the vibration in the Sonicare is visibly more aggressive in its cleaning action without damaging teeth or hurting gums. The vibration hums instead of rattles. Try it -- you'll see what I mean.
As I came to Amazon to shop for my product, I was turned off by the frequent bad reviews about leakage into the battery compartment. I frankly do not know whether that is still a problem, as one reviewer said he believed Sonicare had solved the problem.
When I ordered my brush, I also ordered an inexpensive container of O-Ring lubricant. No need to buy food quality or scuba quality, any lubricant will do. Vaseline may well do the trick, but petroleum is bad on rubber, and since I do not know the material on the Sonicare O-Ring, I thought it better to spend a couple of bucks for a small, inexpensive tube of silicone lubricant. O-Ring lubricants serve three primary purposes: first, it keeps the o-ring supple. Second, it lubricates the surface to make it easier to reassemble the cover without damaging the o-ring when you replace the battery. And third, it prevents leakage. I noticed that the unit I purchased has a flat stand so that this unit is laid on its side when it is not being used, instead of standing upright where any water remaining in the head can drip down and find its way into that battery compartment. I have not had my unit very long, but I intend to watch that battery compartment and will update this review if my brush leaks despite my precautions.

I fully expect, however, that this Sonicare Extreme will outlive the 2 1/2 year warranty.

I did not mention that Sonicare extends their normal 2 year warranty by six months if you go online to register your product. I expect I'll have to tolerate a few emailed special offers for that extra six months, but maybe it will turn out to be a good investment. That's a pretty long warranty for a product that is used as frequently as this thing -- and certainly will outlive the rechargeable units I've been using.
UPDATE: I've now had this unit for about two months, and in that time I've replaced the NiMH batteries twice for re-charging. The brush takes excellent care of my teeth and gums -- aggressive without being destructive. Most importantly, the silicone grease I'm using on the o-ring that seals the battery compartment is keeping that compartment clean and dry. I haven't changed my mind -- expect this product to last its full two and a half year warranty, and beyond, since I can just swap out the batteries. We have two of these in the household and both are working like Swiss watches.

title: I like it a lot, with a couple of caveats
text:
I really enjoy using this oil on my skin. It smells fantastic and seems to absorb quickly, so it doesn’t feel greasy. I can put it on a few minutes before bed, and not worry about getting oil or lotion all over the sheets. I’ve been using it mostly on my legs and arms, but also made a point to use it on my hands and cuticles, and my hands felt great. I think it will be really good this winter as the air gets drier.

I did not, however, like this in my hair. Oils usually work really well in my hair, but I felt like the scent changed almost immediately after putting it on. I smelled a rancid smell, which it does not have in the bottle, and my hair and scalp were clean. Perhaps it’s just my body chemistry, but I was not a fan of this use.

A couple of other things that I wanted to mention that I think are important to know before you buy this:

1. Peppermint and Eucalyptus Essential oils are not recommended on children under the age of six and 10 respectively, so I would not use this on babies or toddlers despite the recommendation on the insert. Children under the age of two should generally avoid topical use of any essential oil. Yes, the oils in this product appear to be highly diluted, but I wouldn’t chance it. They are still smelling it even if you’re not putting it on them.

2. I’m hesitant to use anything with essential oils as an “intimate” lubricant as recommended. Too much potential (in my mind) for mucosal membrane damage, and no, I’m not talking about your nose. Also, oil-based lubricants will break down latex, so be aware of this.

Other than the above concerns I mentioned (which are not concerns if you are using it correctly) I really like using this moisturizer. I will definitely continue to enjoy it.

title: A little goes a long way . . .
text:
I am the kind of shopper who likes to read the reviews and makes my decisions from other people’s experiences. If you are like me you will undoubtedly find this helpful. Let me begin by saying I had a deodorant that was working well for me, but I decided I wanted to make a change and select something more natural. I chose Don’t Sweat It! because of the few and natural ingredients that it contains. When I first tried it, I didn’t think about the fact that this is a different product than what I had been using before and I applied it vigorously. This led to some discomfort under my arms. I had a similar experience, several years ago, from applying too much of a baking soda deodorant each time I used the deodorant. After my first day using the product, I decided to read the label and it was then that I saw it said “Twist open, very lightly swipe and dab under arm. A little goes a long way!” It was then that I realized not only was I applying it incorrectly, but I was using a different product entirely and that I had been automatically applying the same amount of deodorant as before without thinking about what I was doing. On the second day, I followed the instructions and swiped twice lightly under each arm and it worked extremely well. I didn’t have any discomfort at the end of the day and the deodorant worked very well. (I also felt good about using this product.) I plan to continue using this and would recommend it to anyone who is thinking about using it.

Everyone’s body is different, so two swipes for me may be a couple dabs for someone else or it may be three swipes for yet another person. You know your body better than anyone else and it may take more than a day to discover the right amount for you. I found out my formula for success with this deodorant very quickly. It may take you longer. Also, if you have problems with baking soda and essential oils, it says on their label that you can try their unscented product or go to their website for more information.

I hope this helped you in your decision.

title: Nice Peel - Will buy again
text:
I struggle with dull dry skin on my face, especially since I've gotten older. I've used various peels with various levels of success, with some too strong and some too weak. I wasn't sure what to expect.

It said to use a "moderate amount" not sure what that meant from a such a fairly small bottle, so i used a little less than a dime, once I started rubbing it on in a circular motion as directed it immediately started balling up so I squeezed another dollop about the size of a nickel. I've never had a peel ball up instantly like that, I presume it was dead skin lifting off. I've had that happen from a hot microfiber cloth, but the balls were a lot smaller.

After rinsing my skin looked and felt a lot smoother. I have very sensitive skin and after moisturizing I still feel a little tingle, but it's not bad or uncomfortable like other products. I still have a little dull skin on my cheeks under my eyes, so I definitely need to use it again to get the rest of it. The tube does not say how often to repeat the process, but considering my sensitive skin and the lingering tingle I'll wait a day or two before doing it again. Once all the dead skin is removed after a couple of applications, I think i'll only need to use it once a week to keep up maintaining smooth and bright skin.

I'll definitely buy this again!

text:
I bought this because I was wanting to try fiberglass without spending a ton on something I might hate. I definitely do not hate these nails! They are thin and natural looking, and still super strong. I will absolutely continue using fiberglass nails.

BUT... They are a bit of a pain to use, and some of that pain is actual, physical pain from getting fiberglass stuck in your skin. I'd advise using gloves, and will follow my own advice on that going forward. Fiberglass is actual wee little glass fibers which are nearly impossible to see and remove when you get a bit stuck in your skin and can be really irritating and painful. I ended up smearing my hands with tacky glue, letting it dry, and then peeling it off to get rid of the it. It worked pretty well, but yeah, gloves.

The gel in this set cured well, and as I said, my nails are very strong. I used Young Nails Protien Bond and the base coat, and so far no lifting whatsoever, when I usually would start seeing some.

The little LED light is cute, but I wouldn't ever use it for curing nails. I have a better light and I halved the recommending curing times since they're given for the tiny lamp.

title: One professional haircut LAST MARCH 2020
text:
As I write my review on August 7, it has been more than 5 months since I've been to a barber shop. The corona virus could do me in because I have a compromised immune system and I'm an old codger. I bought this cordless cutter thinking I could skip a trip to the barber and go half as often as I normally do, but this cutter has worked so well for me (with just a little help from my wife) that I might just go the entire year skipping the barber shop.

Despite having bursitis in both of my shoulders and arthritis everywhere, I'm able to "manipulate" and maneuver the cutter to give myself a "not too bad looking" haircut. The cutter comes with enough attachments that you can select the depth of the desired cut you need for different areas of hair needing trimming.

I'm impressed with how long the cutter can be turned on and used on a single charge, and the way the cutter is shaped, it is easy to hold. It pretty much conforms to my decrepit hands and is comfortable to hold.

If I were having to make a speech, or giving away a daughter at a wedding, I'd go to a professional barber for a "real" haircut, but for an "old codger" who often doesn't get off of the ranch much these days, this cutter does the job for cutting my own hair, during the "scare" of Covid-19.

title: Worst brand on the market
text:
I bought several brands of Magnetic Eyelashes and liners: Newcally, Yiwamica, CARETHYS, Coolours, and LAMIX. This one, CARATHYS was the worst. The eyelashes looked "unkempt" compared to the others and less natural because the fibers were double layered. The magnets on the back were such poor quality! They had weak magnetic power (compared to Newcally, LAMIX, and Coolours but same as Yiwamica) and they were glued on haphazardly. The spacing was uneven and they were all crooked. Yiwamica had magnet issues too, where the magnets were weak and some even fell off, but at least those lashes looked more natural. This brand was the worst.

Two pros:
--Lashes fibers were thinner so looked more natural compared to the better quality brands and slightly less black
--The liner wasn't too bad. The consistency was actually pretty good, neither goopy nor too liquid, but the lash magnets are bad so not going to keep just for the liner!

I would recommend Newcally for the best quality (but least natural). LAMIX and Coolours are also good choices.

title: Magnets are too weak!!
text:
Update: The top pair in the 234 was my favorite because it's the most natural looking but after 2 uses, one of the magnets fell off! This brand has quality issues. I decided to order many other brands of magnetic lashes (Newcally, LAMIX, Coolours) and I found that the magnets for the Yiwamica's lashes are considerably weaker. The other brands lashes would pop on and when pulled off would pull my skin a little. This brand's magnets do not do that. I have to press the eyelashes on and then corners would dislodge. I thought it was due to the liner but no, it's the magnets! Between the magnets falling off completely and the weak magnets, I'm downgrading from 4 to 2 stars.

As for the styles, I bought 3 sets from this listing: 230, 231, and 234. See my photo.

The 234 is a set of 3 with a natural pair, a denser natural pair same length, and a longest natural pair. The length difference is probably 1mm, very hard to tell on the tray (I didn’t measure with ruler or anything) but you can tell in person when wearing them. I think only the first pair looks truly natural on me for everyday use because I have small Asian hooded eyes. The other two in the 234 tray are sort of natural but I would not use them for day time use.

The 231 has 2 pairs that looked the same as the longest pair in the 234 set...again not natural enough for small eyes for day time use.

The 230 has crisscrossed lashes where it is longer towards the outer corners and shorter towards the inner. These lashes are longer than those in the 231 and 234.

I ended up returning 231 because it was a repeat of my least favorite pair in the 234 set.

The 230 box had quality issues. One of the lash strands was super long on one of the lashes. The 230 set was also glued to the plastic holder instead of magnetized to strips on the tray like the other two sets. When I removed the lashes from the holder, the middle magnet fell off 2 of the lashes!

I also got a eyeliner and 2 lash pair set from the same company. You can see in my photo. That eye liner turned out to be really bad so I returned that.

Instead, I use the Aroama brand of magnetic liner also sold on Amazon (the one with over 1,000 reviews) with these lashes. The magnetics in these lashes are sorta big but since I have to draw the liner really thick for them to stay at all, it’s tough to even notice the magnets. The thick liner could also contribute to the lashes not looking as natural.

I want to mention the magnet spacing is inconsistent across this brand. There are always 5 magnets but some are gapped evenly while others you get 2 magnets on each end and one in the middle with a huge gap on each side. The ends of the lashes do tend to detach from the eye easily for me as compared to the middle so the configuration with 2 magnets on the ends helps me. The spacing is purely up to your preference though. Pay attention to the product photos to see which magnet spacing you would get.

title: So Good My Girlfriend Stole It From Me - Very Good Facial Cleansing Brush
text:
I'm confident more women than men get this brush and it is a little feminine for my style but I wanted to try something to see if I could improve my skin condition. I've only recently started to use a cleansing brush as part of my evening routine after watching the success my daughter had using one on her skin. I decided to give this a try and found it very good ... it was so good in fact that my girlfriend stole it from me!

The brush feels very well manufactured and the design is aesthetically pleasing. I got the brush handle and all of the brush wet and had no issues. I didn't learn until later that some brushes recommend you don't get anything other than the brush head wet. I treated this kind of like I treat a razor. I did not submerge it nor would I. The brush definitely loosens up dirt and oil on your face quickly. I felt the LumaRx had a significant power for scrubbing my face.

The brush comes with multiple brush attachments, to be honest I haven't completely figured out which attachment is best for what job so I use the softer brush. I have used this a few times in the morning before shaving and it does a very good job of helping me get a much closer shave, I believe because it deeply moisturizes the whiskers and helps them stand up better for a clean cut.

The brush comes with a travel bag and charger, the heads are very easy to change and are durable. Charging is quick and I've used it more than a dozen times on one charge.

I think I must have talked too much about how much I liked this brush so my girlfriend decided to start using it and I'm afraid I'm not going to see it again!

Heres the thing though: As one who is fortunate to have some eyebrow already, you MUST comb your brows in the direction you want to use the pen before you apply. Drawing against hairs is self defeating. Also, you must do a little practice on how the lines will go. It isn't mascara, or shadow, or even liner. It takes a bit of practice to get it right. Watch microblading videos...yeah...it's pretty much that, without the pain or permanence...and just as easy to screw up and look awful. (look up "bad microblade" and you'll see what I mean) Not something I plan to use every day, but a wonderful alternative to the permanence and "blue fade" of microblading. Also, I mascara my brows after I use the pen to soften the lines a bit. Have fun! It's definitely a fun product to play with.

title: The Winner!
text:
I haven’t worn mascara in over a year because I just got tired of it flaking, irritating my eyes, globbing two or more lashes together, etc. My lashes are not full but they are long, so mostly I just wanted color, dark gray if possible. Couldn’t find gray, or color only and am too shaky to try dye. So last week, I ordered 6 different brands of black mascara, all at very low cost.
I’ve tried them all now, with one coat, with two coats, with remover pads and oil based remover, sleeping overnight without removing, wearing during swim aerobics, wearing all day working in the yard.
Some made my lashes clump, some made my lashes stiff, hard, some heavily coated, most flaked off during the day, some smeared during my swim aerobics, some itched, some irritated, some were difficult to apply without getting on my skin, some were difficult to get completely off.
The only one that met my needs was QJC Waterproof Mascara.
It was the last to arrive and I was really frustrated by that time with the five others I’d already tried, so I wasn’t very hopeful. But I was happily surprised!
It went on smoothly without clumping. The applicator is dense and just as fat as others, but I easily avoided marking my skin. It lasted throughout a busy day of swim aerobics, grocery shopping, working in the yard without flaking or smudging. My lashes remained soft throughout the day. I left it on overnight and had no flakes or smudges! And my lashes still felt soft and natural looking. It came off easily with eye makeup remover pads on one eye, and oil based liquid on the other. I ran a makeup cleansing cloth over my eyes after I’d cleaned my eyelashes and there was no trace of mascara. Although I did not try to lengthen my eyelashes, it did so without trying. Other reviews have noted it’s lengthening capability.
I’m very pleased with this one. I won’t have to purchase again for a while because it’s a pack of two and very inexpensive!

Her normal hair prep time on school mornings is anywhere from 20 to 30 minutes. She uses a flatiron, because the heated brush I got her won't straighten her hair enough. She has to be really careful, and even so has often burned her fingers and the skin around her face trying to straighten the tiny tight pincurls that encircle her face and head. I have been hunting around for a better, faster solution for her and found it in this wonderful salon quality ceramic heated comb by KingdomCare.

I was originally going to save it for her birthday in the fall, but seeing her daily struggle with the curly locks I opted for an early gifting. I watched her do her hair and noticed that she did not have to use such small segments as she normally does with her flatiron. She was never concerned about her hand getting burned, nor was I. You could touch the outer shell of the heated portion and not be burned. Likewise near the base of the hair, no worries about burning tender facial skin. And the curls disappeared like magic as they skimmed through comb's tines.

Additional features I like about this heating comb are the swiveling cord, the six temperature settings (with lighted buttons to let you know how how the setting is), the smooth feel of the surface and the cool pale pink and silver color of the comb as well as the easy grip surface on the handle. There is an on/off button, heat up/down arrows and temperature displays in both fahrenheit and celsius. This curling comb also reaches higher temperatures than other heated brushes. The one I use tops out lower than the lowest temp on this device. That makes this comb particularly great for thick, wavy hair.

The ceramic heating elements also do a nice job dealing with fly away hairs and static. My granddaughter is really ecstatic with her new beauty tool and is already anticipating all her friends being jealous and wanting to borrow it from her. I definitely award this straightener five stars. It absolutely lives up to its reputation and does not cost a fortune to own.

It’s all bendy and what you do is sort of braid your hair onto/with this. After that, you use the included scrunchies to hold it in place at the bottom.

This sounds all well and good but, maybe it was just me, it was difficult to get my hair twisted correctly onto the rod. My hair is long, reaching about mid back and perfectly straight. If you get it on there right, it comes out looking very nice. It just takes a whole lot of practice. Also, as a side note, if your hair is a little damp, it works better.

This comes with the main curler, two large scrunchies, two smaller scrunchies, two hair clips, and a nice bag to keep everything in. The scrunchies are silk.

This works nicely and it’s worth trying out if you want heatless curls. For me it was difficult to get the knack of but if you are good with hair, which I am just not, you might find it quite easy from the start.

title: It's good
text:
This Melao lavender exfoliant foot peel works very well. The box contains one set of booties for one time use. It’s real simple to use these. You have to start off by cleaning your feet well. It doesn’t hurt to give them a bit of a soak for a time as well beforehand. Just to get them good ready. Next, you place the booties on your feet. It’s recommended that you put socks over the booties to hold them firmly in place since you have to wear them for an hour. I did just that and think that’s a mighty fine recommendation to follow. When that hour is up, you take all that off your feet and give your feet a good washing with soap and water. Now comes the waiting game. At first, I thought they did absolutely nothing.For days, I thought they did nothing. Then, around the 4th/5th day my feet just started to peel. They were shedding skin. It was so weird! They continued to do that for a few days and when it was all over my feet did look and feel really nce for quite some time. Just remember to keep moisturizing to keep them looking and feeling nice for a long time after.

The thing about this product is that you can’t expect instant results. It takes a few days and you have to still use the same moisturizers and stuff you were using on your feet, or at least I did. I have really dry feet in spots and I despise it so to have something actually work for a little while was great. You would have to use these every so often though, I think, to keep them as nice.
At this time, when I type this, there isn’t a price listed for these so I can’t tell you if it’s worth it or not but they work well and could be.

title: Cordless or corded snipping
text:
I was looking at this as an extension to the [[ASIN:B000EG8HLE Philips Norelco BG2020 Bodygroom Shaver]]. Not really its intended purpose but it does work pretty well in that role as long as you are careful. Emphasis on the being careful; it can, and will, grab loose skin.

Overall I'm pleased with it. It cuts through hair quickly and easily making it easy for quick touch up trims. It's also fairly quiet, much quieter than my electric shaver so it doesn't affect my hearing when trimming sideburns and hair that's grown longer than my ears. It will also operate in either corded or cordless mode, handy when the battery dies.

Only a few negatives from my view:
-The charging LED in the handle does not shut off when the unit is charged. It is lit the entire time it's plugged in. Little annoying considering almost very rechargeable device will let you know when it has completed charging.
- It does not charge at the same time you are using it while plugged in. Not really a big deal, just something to be aware of.
- Only the head portion can be rinsed; the base / battery can not get wet. Again, not really a big deal.
- Hair trimmings get stuck in the lubricant grease inside the head. Not a lot, only a few very small pieces, but if you're a perfectionist it can be a little aggravating.

I'm expecting this will also work well to trim out the tufts of overgrown toe fur that my cat gets. I can, and do, trim with scissors periodically but it takes a bit of time due to being careful. The longer it takes the more annoyed he gets. Using this I should be able to trim the fur much quicker so he gets less annoyed. Less annoyed cat == less annoyed human. We both win!

Update: Dec 1, 2010
15 months later and I'm still using this. Does a fantastic job of keeping the hair around my ears trimmed just enough so that it isn't touching or rubbing. Very quick and quiet. It still irks me a little bit that it doesn't tell you when charging is complete. The other nitpicks I've gotten over.

I can't say how well it works on trimming toe fur on a long haired cat. The shaver is in one room and when I see that he needs a trim we're in a different one. I did use it once to snip out some matted up fur and it did a decent job.

title: Have you tried everything else?
text:
I write this review on another brand of this exact same soap. However, I found the price to be better and quality is exactly the same. I have tried every single product I could get my hands on to clear up an ongoing infection on my neck that put me in the emergency room. I thought it was shingles and was even diagnosed as such. The Doctors gave me antibiotics and sent me on my way. Over a year later, whatever it is/was kept on spreading. I have dealt with this nightmare and it has consumed my life and sent me into a terrible depression. My skin was itching, my neck would burn if I turned it too much, it was sore all the time and I would get these constant breakouts, like acne but I knew they were not acne. I have never felt so miserable.

In the past I have tried turmeric (internally and as a mask), green tea, sulfur, benzoyl peroxide, pro-biotics, internal oregano, tea tree oil, manuka oil, manuka honey, antibiotics, changing my entire diet to eat healthy and lots of fruit and vegetables... The list goes on and on and not one thing helped. Not ONE!

Then, about a month ago, I was researching folliculitis and many of the symptoms matched what was going on with me. I do not remember how I stumbled upon this soap but I thought, what the hell. I tried everything else, lets see if this does ANYTHING at all. It has been about a month now and my skin is nearly completely healed. The itching is nearly subsided completely, The burning sensation is GONE. My skin is starting to feel normal again. I prayed and prayed for the pain to just stop and now, finally it has.

You need to give this soap a try. I will never let my friends, family or anyone I ever come in contact with go through what I went through now that I have learned. If you do some research online, start with Wikipedia and you will see what I now know.

Be careful, this soap does burn quite a bit and takes time to get used to but the burn never damaged my skin, I can actually feel it working. I am grateful I finally found something that helped me get better.

Florida Water is iconic and Murray and Lanman's is the most famous Florida Water available. It's light, refreshing, citrusy, outdoorsy (sic.) and a pleasure to splash on after a shave. However, if you want to kick your Florida Water up a notch, I highly recommend adding at least 8-10g of menthol crystals to a new bottle. Pro Tip: pulverize the menthol crystals in mortar and pestle. Add a tablespoon of the Florida Water to the powder. Mix until dissolved. Use a small perfume funnel to add the mixture back into the bottle.

title: Quality soap, inexpensive, questionable scent...
text:
I purchased an Arko stick for travel, to use with my [[ASIN:B003B3UAM6 Wee Scot Best Badger Shave Brush 70mm shave brush by Simpson]]. The combination gave me a great BSS while on the road, but I am not a fan of the scent. It reminds me of that old bathroom soap that ground the soap cake into your palm like parmesan cheese, the smell, that is. Have to say that I don't care for it. Also, when you open the stick, you will have no choice but to either loosely wrap it back up after use, or, as I do, store the open stick in a plastic bag. A better option would be a plastic tube with a cap. Naturally, that would affect the price negatively. These days there are many travel shaving soap options, so while Arko will give you a smooth shave, if the scent isn't your thing, you can easily find something else.
Recommended for its shaving qualities, NOT for the scent.

text:
We have owned different Oral B power toothbrushes over the years with the latest being the 1000. I have no complaints with the 1000 it works.

When determining if one should purchase the 4000 or the 1000, one needs to look at the additional features the 4000 provides.

If you have sensitive gums then you will need to purchase the 4000, there is a gentle mode. Additionally, I would not recommend purchasing the floss action heads if you have sensitive gums.
While there is an in handle display in the 4000, it is not a digital display. It is a light next to the feature you are currently selecting

I do not see any difference when using the polishing mode in the 4000, however, I do not have stains to determine if the feature works.

The one annoyance for me with the 4000 is that I accidentally change the mode instead of turning off the brush from time to time because the button are close enough to do this.
While I recommend the Oral B 4000, I would suggest using the 1000 if you do not have sensitive or stained teeth.

title: Decent product!
text:
So I don’t own a blow dryer or a hair straightener. I know. I bought this to hopefully replace the need for both of them. Pictured: my hair styled when damp, my hair styled and natural side-by-side, and my hair styled when dry (tie-dye shirt).

Some pros: I have very wavy, long, fine hair, but a ton of it, and can dry/style my hair in under 30 minutes with this. Yes the brush size is huge, but with how much hair I have, I need it to be large. The style it produced was beautiful! I will be keeping this for sure!

Some cons: I deducted a star mainly because this brush doesn’t get very hot. I guess this could be a pro since it won’t damage your hair as much over time. But for me, I noticed that some parts of my hair were still wavy, and that the style didn’t hold perfectly over time.

Some tips: definitely use this tool on damp hair. It semi-straightened my dry hair, but the style did not hold over time and my hair went right back to wavy in an hour. I had to go over my damp hair a few times, but make sure to maintain tension when you pull. That’s the best way I was able to get my hair straight. Another reason I deducted a star was because I still feel like I need a flat iron to do touch ups—around my roots specifically. But this product is definitely better than using a flat iron all over!

Verdict: worth $20! Glad I purchased.

title: Nice exfoliating shampoo
text:
I'm a HUGE Eva NYC fan (the Mane Magic line is better than most salon products I've tried), so I was excited to try this as soon as I saw it. My scalp is touchy, and occasionally flakes.

The salt crystals are much larger than I expected, and that (probably combined with the thickness of my hair) made it a little challenging to distribute across the scalp at first; I added a splash of water and a little more product than I would use with a normal shampoo, and that did the trick. It lathers nicely after it emulsifies and really does make my hair feel squeaky clean.

I can't say whether it makes my ends feel dry because I always condition well; I generally follow this with the Therapy Session Mask, Mane Magic Primer, and Satin Dream Leave-In Cream from the same brand. Unfortunately it didn't do anything good for my root volume (my hair is very heavy, so that's common), but it didn't make it look greasy at the roots either.

I'm not sure how effective it would be against serious scalp flaking from something like psoriasis, but if you need an occasional round of clarifying and exfoliation to fend off light flakes and product build-up, this is a good product to try.

Side note: the first tube I received recommended following this shampoo with the Wellness Monster Mask (which I haven't come across). Subsequent tubes have recommended the Therapy Session Mask instead. Not sure if Wellness Monster is a discontinued mask, or one that hasn't yet been released, but the Wellness Monster tube also looked less filled than the others. I kind of assume it was older and the product had settled somewhat.

title: I can work with this!
text: I was able to cut the front folded rubber hairline off of this and make it blend fairly well with having a bit of my natural hair pulled out at the hairline. There is still a visible line because as you know, it's not lace, but a thin piece of rubber simulated scalp, so there's an edge, but on this wig I got lucky that the edge layed flat, so even though there's a line, it's a flat line as opposed to a lifted line which would look much more obvious. I've worn it in public, around my family and no one noticed it's a wig. It passed my test! I did sew wig combs in the sides and back though because the first time I wore it, there was slippage (even though I wore it with a wig grip), but since sewing on the combs, it doesn't budge. The hair itself is really pretty. It does shed quite a bit, but so does my natural hair. I'm used to it. It was fine putting some heat on it, just be careful...not too hot. Of course it tangles after wearing it for a day, but tangles come out just fine as long as you're gentle. The style of the hair is so pretty, and if you don't mind working with it a little (cutting the rubber, plucking the part, adding combs, etc.), it's worth the cost and has the potential to look fairly natural. Sorry about the graininess of the photo due to low lighting. Other photos I took made the wig take on a reddish hue, so I didn't post those here, but it truly is a light/medium brown with darker (not black) roots.

title: Cute with a couple issues
text:
This wig looks really cute, and I was able to get it to mostly blend with my natural gray hair around my face and with my widow's peak, which is pretty hard to blend in with a lot of wigs. I don't like to use any kind of glue or tape, so I depend on a wig grip and bobby pins to hold everything in place. This fit my head pretty well, and I have an average size head, but I think slightly larger heads would fit too. I'm not sure it would do too well if you have really long and thick hair, as it might take up too much space in the cap. When I had it on, I didn't notice the tracks, but when it was off I thought they were pretty noticable, and I was a little worried. Also you know how on some wigs, they add those short annoying hairs that inevitably end up poking through the longer ones and looking weird? Yep, I noticed the hair towards the back of the cap does that. Coincidentally, that's the place where the tracks are most visible as well.
The thing I like about it, is the actual hair, and the color, the texture, and the ability to flip it from side to side (even though it's parted in the middle. The style of it is most like my natural hair of any wig that I've purchased so far. I did add some dry shampoo. The color looks really awesome indoors. Outside in the daylight, it is a little much. It looks pretty white outdoors, but has a nice silvery-gray color indoors. So there are some negatives, but I could see wearing this as a daily wear wig. It didn't tangle too badly after a full day of wear... even with me running my fingers through it and flipping it like I do. I was easily able to tidy it up by finger combing at the end of the day. I wish the back side was slightly longer because the front that frames your face is longer and the waves in the back can look a little shaggy compared to the slightly curlier waves in the front. Overall, it's still cute, but I think the price is too much for this short wig. It should be closer to the $20 range. I'd love to own a 22-24" version of this in the same color or even a slightly darker gray or gray mix.

text:
I actually really like this palette. I love the banana color. I have very pale skin, so finding a highlighting shade that is actually lighter than my skin is really hard. This shade is MUCH lighter, but it is definitely lighter. I LOVE that there is such a variety of darker shades, it makes it possible for me to bring out some features more than the other when I contour, which isn't an option for a lot of other palettes. The powder goes on very smooth and effortlessly. In earlier reviews it states that this doesn't have good coverage, but it's a contour palette, it isn't meant to cover anything. I don't need to use much of the powder for it to show on my skin, I definitely don't want "harsh contour lines" so I only use about 3 brush strokes of each color. My highlighter came broken due to Amazon's poor packaging, but I was able to use the broken powder to test out the product before my replacement comes. I have tried a few other contour palettes in the past and this one goes on the best, while at the same time using the least amount of product.
I was VERY excited to receive this in one of their recent promotions, and I definitely recommend to anyone that is starting out with Contouring or anyone that just wants to try out a new palette for a good price.

title: Different from what I expected
text:
Spa-Da Immunity Support Soap 6pk | 7 Essential Oils Clinically Evaluated to Boost Immunity and Protect | Moisturizes with Sweet Almond Oil | Healthy PH for Skin Microbiome | Handmade in Ohio-

Pros-
Great for exfoliating
Hydrating
Skin feels great after usage
Made in the USA

Cons-
The scent is very strong of clove (too much so for me) It's the only scent I can smell from the soap.
Breaks down very fast
Fewer suds than traditional soap ( more suds than I would have thought but still less)

I was a bit thrown off by this soap. Before getting it I was thinking it was going to be like regular soap but when you see it it’s anything but regular soap. My roommate and I were both a bit confused thinking perhaps these were bath bombs because the look is similar to bath bombs more than it is to bar soap. I had to revisit the listing to double-check that it is meant to be used as soap.

Usage is interesting. It does break down very quickly though it stays intact long enough to use as bar soap. You just don’t get many washes out of each bar. With water, it does suds up a good amount which I like. It also gets a bit milky looking and the gritty texture does exfoliate too.

After using it I like the feeling of it on my skin. My skin feels a little tingly, refreshed, and soft. So it does work well for me as a soap but it just doesn’t last long.

The scent is not my favorite at all. Some might enjoy the scent but it’s very strongly clove-scented. It’s a bit too overbearing for my tastes. The scent also seems to last on my skin for a little longer than normal bar soap would. If I was more fond of the scent this would be a good thing.

Overall it’s a decent product but it’s not really for me. I just don’t love the scent and it’s a bit too different from normal bar soap for me. I love the exfoliating ability of this soap. That is the one area I really liked and I would buy this if I found a scent I enjoyed. The price is reasonable given that you get 6 bars. I would say they last maybe 1/3rd to 1/4th of the length of most bar soaps and that might be a stretch.

title: Feels amazing but pricey
text:
FOR BELOVED ONE Melasleep Brightening Lumi's key Bio-Cellulose Facial Treatment Mask (33g x 1PC)

This is an impressive gel face mask. I love the feeling of this mask. It’s a heavy gel mask that is anything but dry. It’s extremely refreshing.

I will say the directions are brief. When you take it out it’s tri-folded (the one image above are the two outer layers and the mask was in between those). It does rip if you aren’t cautious with it. There are 3 layers. Once you gently unfold it you peel off the first layer. Then apply to the face and after doing so peel off the outside cover. It is much easier if you pull out the eye holes and mouth hole before placing on your face. It does have a fair amount of staying power once it’s in place for a minute. Directions state to leave it on for 10-15 minutes. I left mine on for probably about 20 minutes.

The end result was great. My skin felt clean, rejuvenated, and soft. I really am impressed with the results given my hesitation to try a brand I wasn’t familiar with. I wish I had more of these because I would love to use them on a regular basis but the cost is a bit unrealistic to me.

Thus the one negative with this mask. The price point is very steep. I’ve had many masks that worked very well for much less. Now I did have a particularly great result from this mask so don’t get me wrong it may very well be worth the money to some. I’m just not one of those people that could justify it to myself. However, I do love the feeling I have after using it. I am not going to knock the product rating for the price point because that is really the only thing that I don’t like here. The product itself is really good and I’m happy with the results. I would just reiterate that the listing is for a single mask.

Instructions do say to use a file to rough up nail surface first which I did not do this time but does make it faster
First pic of my nail (gel polish over clear tips using solid nail tips gel and uv light to attach them instead of nail glue) is before remover
Second pic is one coat of remover about 5 seconds after application
Third pic is second extremly thick coat probably third and fourth coat also. Applied right over first one a few seconds after application

If I didn't have the tips and it was just straight gel polish I'm sure I could use less and it would take less time. But I wouldn't use this for that I do not think. Haven't yet. I should add I have had no damage to my natural using this stuff or pain on my natural nail. On my skin doesn't feel so hot but it does wash away and there's no redness or discomfort once washed off. title: Pros and Cons to Consider
text:
I have very dense, thick, and long 4C hair, so my texture is the most coarse texture of hair to possibly test the durability of this blower-dryer comb. Anyone that has coarse or thick hair such as yours truly, likely runs into the same problem as me when you blow dry your hair after a washing. The dang blow-dryer comb keeps popping off and/or the teeth bends and snaps off. So annoying! Since this is very expensive for a blow-dryer comb, I'm sure ladies will appreciate this critical review before purchasing. Here are the pros and cons I've come across.

Pros...The material is the highest grade of plastic (not at all rubber) I have seen in a blow-dryer comb. It appears to be equivalent to the "plastic" material cooking utensils are made of, so the teeth does not easily bend/break. The finer and less dense your hair is, the longer the life-time you will have this comb. If you attach it securely, the comb actually works without popping off.

Cons...This seems to only work for dryers with a narrow barrel, and not so much for the dryers that has a bubble shape. It will pop off dryers with a bubble shaped barrel, because it will be impossible to secure it on a nozzle tip that is not cylinder-shaped. All you need is a phillips screwdriver to attach it. Since I have 4C hair, I did actually notice slight bending of a couple teeth, and the bending increased after a 3rd usage. After my 3rd hair drying, I tried to hand-bend the teeth back in place, and 2 snapped off! $40 bucks (cost and shipping) down the drain :-( Also, what you don't know until you see it in person is that there is a metal bar inside the comb, that is being raked against your hair as you are combing it, which will eventually cause heat damage with prolonged usage, especially if you dry your hair on high.

My overall assessment is that, yes it worked better that expected. Although 2 teeth broke on mine and others slightly bent, I plan on buying another one to have on-hand, as I currently have not come across any better options. But, I'm going to take a break from this comb for a while, and try drying my hair with a paddle brush and my dryer because the thought of that metal bar inside the Willie Morrow comb, raking against my hair with every usage is alarming, and will surely heat damage my hair.

I started to spray this on the brushes but decided that maybe wasn't the best approach for my situation. So I got a small bowl, filled it with maybe 1/4 cup of water and put about 1/4 of the bottle of the makeup cleaner in the bowl. I let them sit for about 24 hours, agitating them a few different times. I then took them and rinsed them and worked them with clean water until it ran clear - maybe 5 minutes of effort. And now I have sparkley clean brushes again! The whites are bright white again! I apparently had a couple clumps of foundation in my one brush and this got those right out too. I feel much better knowing my brushes are clean again and now I can use the rest of this for maintenance as well as on my powered makeups!

text:
Before purchasing I had read the reviews and believed any issues were isolated and decided to purchase. Unfortunately I was only able to get 4 small tattoos out of the entire pack. Printing was relatively simple and the ink did not run or bleed out. I used photo quality and matte paper for my settings.

The issue is with the adhesive. For the tattoos to work you have to first print the item on the paper; then using the clear adhesive sheet cover the tattoo. All the clear sheet is used for is a transfer medium to move the adhesive onto the image. Where I ran into the problem was getting the adhesive film to release from the plastic sheet and remain on the image. Separating the image side and the clear plastic sheeting resulted in varied degrees of torn images, half the adhesive sticking, or the entire image sticking to the clear sheet

One tip would be to have someone hold down the adhesive/image side as you remove the clear backing. This has its own set of problems since the adhesive side sticks to your hand and gets stretched out or bubbles up.

In summary the idea is great but the adhesive needs to release from its medium easier to make the product more user friendly.

title: The Closest Shave I've Ever Had
text:
I have just used this razor to attain the closest shave of my life. This was done with Every Man Jack Natural Menthol Shaving Gel. My previous best shave was had with an Edwin Jagger DE89 with a blue Personna blade and green Proraso shaving soap. I have not been able to reliably repeat those results with the DE89 and have been using Harry's ever since. My results with them have been reliably good, but their product lineup has recently become rather feminine for my tastes.

Compared to Harry's, the Every Man Jack cartridges seem more aggressive. While this results in a closer shave, it also causes skin irritation more quickly. Those doing single-pass shaves with the grain have little to worry about, but those of us who prefer multi-pass shaves need to exercise care. When doing a multi-pass shave, first go with the grain, then across the grain, and then finally against the grain. Do not ever go directly against the grain with this razor.

I currently plan to continue using this razor, but will be experimenting with different gels and face lotions from this company.

text:
This heatless curler is ok, it’s as described and curls hair without having to utilize a curling iron. I find that it works best when using a light mist of water from a spray bottle and a texturizing spray.

It’s somewhat easy to use, but because it’s made of a silky material, it tends to slide around on my head and not stay in place.

It also doesn’t come with a headband to help keep hair wrapped and secure. It’s a bulkier wrap and leaves the top strands of hair looser which can cause the curls to not be as defined as they could be.

I started by putting the wrap at the top of my head, claw clipped it in place and moved strands of hair from the back of my head, underneath to the front and combined it with strands from the front, then continued to wrap the strands of hair around the wrap. I repeated this on each side until I was done. I used the hair ties at the ends to secure my hair in place. Getting strands of hair from the back to the front in sections can be a little complicated. With practice, it gets easier.

I let it sit in my hair overnight, it worked as described but left wavy/ loose curls rather than tight curls. It’s a good alternative for heat free curls.

title: Note that slices are not full masks
text:
Each pouch has 12 pineapple ring shaped slices you can stick on your face. It is not enough to cover my face and I can wear the average sheet mask.

If you have used circular cucumber eye masks that various brands make, you will find these masks to be similar. You are receiving small rounds in a packet rather than a full sheet mask.

However what is awkward is that unlike cucumber eye sheet masks, you get 12 slices rather than just 2. While this seems like it would be better, in reality is that means you need to commit to using all 12 slices of fruit in one go because there isn’t an easy way to reseal the mask package. It doesn’t come in a resealable pouch.

Because you end up with 12 slices of mask to use you end up covering maybe half your face with slices and you’re basically doing more for less mask. The instructions do say this mask can be used anywhere on the body but I don’t know how that would work in practice. What areas need sheet masking and where will the rounds stick?

I think if Kocostar had made the slice line of masks into a fruit salad deal with multiple slices of fruit per pouch that would’ve made more sense. If they had sold these masks as 12-120 rounds in a container like many eye masks are sold, that also would’ve made sense.

I think if you intend on sharing these masks with others (Eg six friends each taking a pair of slices) or want to store the opened packages or want to use masks to target specific areas of your face or body this could be a good purchase.

These mini masks were moisturizing but dried out faster than a full size sheet mask. I don’t know if that’s due to size or formula.

title: Affordable & Pretty
text:
[[VIDEOID:c7ea1ada61f6bc13ccf9a564082e2c55]] I have relaxed hair & decided to order the 10 inch kinky straight clip in extensions. I hoped the kinky texture would be similar to my own hair but it was not. In my opinion, this feels like Indian hair that has been crimped. Very silky, very soft, & affordable so I'm not mad. I haven't noticed any shedding and I only needed to use 3 pieces since I was only trying to add a little length. The clips are very secure feeling in my hair & it was super easy to install myself. I am definitely a newbie to hair extensions so if you're nervous about being able to do this yourself, don't be!! I will say the hair did smell like burnt hair. Ya know the salon smell with all the hot tools on? Yeah that's the smell lol. Also I will note that it is very difficult to straighten the hair from the weft to about 5 inches down. If I would've known the hair wasn't a truly kinky texture, I would have gone with the regular straight. Overall I'm very happy with the product! I recommend highly.

Oh and sidenote: just for those who may be wondering. You can totally put your hair up with these clip ins. I do suggest getting a longer length though for a ponytail or high bun. No less than 14 inches in my opinion. Also if you're looking to add fullness to your hair, I'd recommend buying 2 sets. As stated earlier, I just wanted a little length in the back b/c my hair is already super thick so one set worked perfect for me.

2) The charging is just "okay". I made it through a complete round (1st time), and into one underarm weeks later. I was almost finished with the first when it died. I had to wait until the next day to finish. That was a bit irritating but given the price, it's to be expected.

3) Perfect size. I have small hands so I really wasn't wanting some bulky device that weighed a ton. This is small and light. Big plus!

Overall, for the price and outcome, it was WELL worth it. I almost bought a $200 device but decided I'd test the waters with what an epilator was to begin with. Don't waste your money unless you're wanting to do your legs or a bigger project. This baby works great! Not great on the legs though. I tried it. I'll stick to shaving those.

title: Now I'm too sexy
text:
Now that I bought and used the T980, my cool slacker goatee is attracting too many women. I'm not getting any rest.

Naturally, a product that causes grief should be down-rated, but I won't here because this shaver is just doing its job.

And, we all like things with "turbo" in the description, however loosely that term is applied. It makes it go faster with a cool noise, so even in a shaver that is attractive to many.

Electric shavers for beards sure beat the heck out of scissors! The Norelco has a wide range of cutting depths and my beard comes out a uniform length. I did not feel any pulling or other discomfort. The charge seems to last for days and the charger itself, like the shaver, is a decent and modern design.

The little detail cutter is easy to attach and does a great job of defining the beard area and also clipping any stray hairs under the nose where the big cutter head cannot reach.

Some people think the closest cutting position is still not close enough for that short-stubble look and that does seem to be the case. I don't want mine that close, but I understand those who do and I take off a star for brotherly solidarity. Actually, I'm sure that if it was to cut more closely, that would take it into the realm of regular shavers, an expensive world of high-tech blades and lubricants. Actually, if you press down a little, you can get closer.

The turbo thing works well. It vacuums almost every hair into the storage chamber. I didn't expect the vacuum action to work so well. I think the turbo button should be the only button, but there it is. The non-turbo setting is less noisy...

The parts detach easily and the little supplied brush works well to clean it out. The little travel pouch is nice.

The T980 works just as it should, for me, and the price is reasonable. I think it will last a long time and I am glad I bought it.

As for the women, I did exaggerate. One did make a favorable comment which is one more than before. That is an improvement, eh?

I agree with most of the other reviews. This is the best electric shaver I've ever had--lightyears better than the Braun Syncro I was using before. The description said that the bristles on this brush were boar bristles.

First problem I noticed was the handle was shorter than I was used to. I am a short average build guy and I have some difficulty reaching my entire back easily with it. Second issue, the bristles are some sort of soft plastic not boar as advertised. The bristles are tightly packed which is nice but very soft. They didn't irritate my skin like some but the softness left me questioning how clean my back was getting. The tightly packed bristles seem like a great feature but after you use it a couple of times you realize that it makes air tough to get through the bristles so the brush takes longer to dry than most. If you don't really sling the remaining water out of them and/or pat down with a cloth the brush may still be damp the next time you go to use it which doesn't seem hygienic. The last issue I have with this back brush is there are no grips or non-slip material where you hold it. It can become kind of slippery and cumbersome when the handle gets wet.

This does seem to be a well made brush that should last a long time, it just wasn't for me. It is definitely better than the the plastic back brushes you find in most retail stores. My Mom loves it. She kept hers and I was easily able to get return authorization through Amazon with no issues for mine. Going back to a wooden natural bristle brush. Sometimes it's better to stick with what you know.
